title: Gene Ontology (GO), basic edition
perspective: GO Consortium (academic, international; molecular biology and model-organism databases)
notes: PURL 302 to current.geneontology.org/ontology/go-basic.obo (build 2026-08-05, data-version releases/2026-07-26). Basic = acyclic: relations limited to is_a, part_of, regulates, negatively_regulates, positively_regulates; relations crossing the three aspects removed (GO download page). OBO 1.2; [Term] stanzas, then 5 [Typedef] stanzas at the end of the file (part_of, regulates, negatively_regulates, positively_regulates, has_ontology_root_term). Tags: id, name, namespace (biological_process, molecular_function, cellular_component), def with dbxref list, synonym with EXACT/BROAD/NARROW/RELATED, is_a, relationship, xref (RHEA, Reactome, MetaCyc, EC, Wikipedia, KEGG_REACTION...), alt_id, subset (GO slims), comment, is_obsolete with replaced_by/consider, property_value. Roots GO:0008150, GO:0003674, GO:0005575. Also go-basic.json(.gz) (obographs). GO asks users to cite the release date.

title: ChEBI ontology, full edition (chebi.obo.gz)
perspective: EMBL-EBI (intergovernmental European research institute, Hinxton UK; biology-oriented chemistry)
update: monthly releases (README: current folder regenerated with each release; nightly/ folder daily); release 255 of 2026-09-09
notes: Gzip of chebi.obo (270,898,581 B uncompressed; PURL http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/chebi.obo). ChEBI 2.0, built with ROBOT templates. Tags: id (CHEBI:n), name, def, subset (1:STAR/2:STAR/3:STAR curation level), synonym with scopes EXACT/RELATED and types IUPAC:NAME, BRAND:NAME, http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/chebi/INN; xref with lower-case bioregistry prefixes (cas, kegg.compound, pubmed, lincs.smallmolecule, reaxys, wikipedia.en...); is_a; relationship with CURIEs labelled by [Typedef] stanzas at the end of the file (RO:0000087 has role, RO:0018038 has functional parent, RO:0018033 is conjugate base of, RO:0018034 is conjugate acid of, RO:0018036 is tautomer of, RO:0018039 is enantiomer of, RO:0018040 has parent hydride, BFO:0000051 has part); property_value chemrof:mass, monoisotopic_mass, charge, generalized_empirical_formula, smiles_string, inchi_string, inchi_key_string; alt_id. languages=3 is an estimate: English names plus WHO INN synonyms in Latin and Spanish/Italian forms (e.g. gemcitabinum, gemcitabina) that carry no language tag. Caveat: the ontology README once calls the licence 'CC Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0' but its LICENSE file, the OBO header (terms:license) and the OBO Foundry registry all say CC BY 4.0; attribution should name ChEBI and the release number.

title: ChEBI ontology, lite edition (chebi_lite.obo.gz)
perspective: EMBL-EBI (intergovernmental European research institute, Hinxton UK; biology-oriented chemistry)
notes: Gzip of chebi_lite.obo (55,411,092 B; PURL http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/chebi/chebi_lite.obo). 'Only ids, name, subsets and relationships' (README): id, name, subset (star level), is_a, relationship (RO CURIEs), alt_id, a few def lines; no synonyms and no xrefs, which this pipeline wants, so prefer chebi-full. Middle option chebi_core.obo.gz (35,806,679 B) adds definitions and chemical properties but still no synonyms/xrefs. README spells the files chebi-lite/chebi-core; the real file names use underscores. Same licence caveat as chebi-full.

title: Uberon multi-species anatomy ontology, basic edition
perspective: Uberon/OBO community (academic, international; comparative anatomy across animals)
notes: PURL redirects to github.com/obophenotype/uberon/releases/latest/download/uberon-basic.obo. 'Excludes external ontologies and most relations' (OBO registry). Tags: id, name, def, synonym with scopes and types (OMO:0003011 latin term, OMO:0003000 abbreviation, HUMAN_PREFERRED, DEVELOPMENTAL, SENSU...), xref (FMA, EMAPA, MA, SCTID, Wikipedia, UMLS, NCIT, BTO, MESH, GAID, VHOG... - rich crosswalks), is_a, relationship (part_of, develops_from, present_in_taxon/never_in_taxon pointing to NCBITaxon ids, immediate_transformation_of...), subset, is_obsolete/replaced_by/consider. languages=2: English plus Latin anatomical terms marked by synonym type OMO:0003011.

title: Cell Ontology (CL), basic edition
perspective: CL/OBO community (academic, international; cell types across species)
notes: 'Basic version, no inter-ontology axioms' (OBO registry): about 3,530 CL terms, links to UBERON anatomy dropped (use cl.obo with merged imports if needed). Tags: id, name, namespace, def, synonym (EXACT/RELATED/BROAD/NARROW), xref (FMA, ZFA, BTO, CALOHA, KUPO, MESH, FBbt, ILX...), is_a, relationship (mostly RO:0002202 develops_from; a few BFO:0000050 part_of), subset, property_value, creation_date, is_obsolete/replaced_by/consider.

title: Human Disease Ontology (DO)
publisher: Disease Ontology project, Institute for Genome Sciences, University of Maryland School of Medicine
perspective: DO project (academic, US; NIH/NHGRI-funded; human disease by etiology)
notes: PURL redirects to raw.githubusercontent.com/DiseaseOntology/HumanDiseaseOntology/main/src/ontology/doid.obo - a branch head, not a release asset; record data-version (releases/2026-08-31) with the bytes. OBO edition omits the equivalent-class axioms (OBO registry). Tags: id (DOID:n), name, def (url: sources), synonym (mostly EXACT), xref (MIM, ORDO, UMLS_CUI, MESH, GARD, ICD10CM, ICD9CM, ICDO, NCI, SNOMEDCT_US_<release-date> - the SNOMED prefix embeds a release date, normalise it), is_a, subset (DO_cancer_slim, NCIthesaurus...), alt_id, disjoint_from, is_obsolete/replaced_by, created_by/creation_date; no relationship lines in the sampled range.

title: Mondo Disease Ontology
perspective: Monarch Initiative (academic consortium, US/international; merges OMIM, Orphanet, DO, NCIt, GARD into one disease hierarchy)
notes: PURL redirects to the v2026-09-01 release asset. mondo.obo embeds thousands of imported non-MONDO terms (GO, HP, CHEBI, CL, ENVO, FOODON...) used in logical definitions: keep only id prefix MONDO, or take mondo-simple.obo (47,608,279 B, PURL http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/mondo/mondo-simple.obo, MONDO terms only, no references to external terms). OBO edition 'omits equivalence axioms; xrefs can be used as proxy for equivalence': xref qualifiers {source="MONDO:equivalentTo"} mark exact matches (OMIM, Orphanet, DOID, NCIT, MESH, UMLS, MEDGEN, GARD, icd11.foundation, SCTID, NANDO...), also property_value skos:exactMatch. Tags: id, name, def, synonym (scopes + types such as ABBREVIATION), xref, is_a with source qualifiers, relationship with named properties (excluded_subClassOf is NOT a hierarchy edge; disease_has_feature, disease_arises_from_structure, has_material_basis_in_germline_mutation_in...), subset (rare, orphanet_rare, gard_rare, otar...), is_obsolete/replaced_by/consider. A Japanese translation exists only as mondo-international.owl.

title: Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO)
publisher: Human Phenotype Ontology Consortium / Monarch Initiative
perspective: HPO Consortium (academic, international, led from The Jackson Laboratory; clinical genetics)
license: HPO licence (custom): free use with citation and version display; content and logical relationships may not be altered
notes: Not an open licence: the HPO page lists three conditions - acknowledge and cite the HPO Consortium, show the date/version of HPO files displayed publicly, and do not alter the content or the logical relationships of the files; services must display an acknowledgement. The file header (terms:license) points to https://hpo.jax.org/app/license, a single-page app that returns 404 to curl, so the text was read at human-phenotype-ontology.github.io. Usable read-only with attribution; merging or crosswalk edits risk breaching the no-alteration clause. Tags: id, name, def, synonym with types layperson, uk_spelling, abbreviation, plural_form, obsolete_synonym; xref (UMLS, MEDDRA, NCIT, Fyler...), is_a, alt_id, subset, comment, is_obsolete/replaced_by/consider; no relationship lines. hp-international.obo (22,476,318 B) adds translations in 12 languages (cs, tr, nl, fr, es, ja, zh, pt, de, it, nna, tw - counted from hp-international.owl tags) but OBO drops most language tags; use hp-international.owl (209,428,804 B) for tagged labels.

title: Environment Ontology (ENVO)
perspective: ENVO/OBO community (academic, international; environments, biomes and habitats for genomics and ecology)
notes: PURL redirects to raw.githubusercontent.com/EnvironmentOntology/envo/master/envo.obo (branch head; data-version releases/2026-06-26). Includes about 835 imported CHEBI terms: keep id prefix ENVO, or use envo/subsets/envo-basic.obo (2,034,421 B, ENVO terms only, readable relation names, but no data-version line). Tags: id, name, def, synonym (all four scopes), xref (FTT, Geonames, TGN, EcoLexicon, SWEETRealm, LTER, SPIRE, CMECS, NLCD, URLs - useful place and biome crosswalks), is_a, intersection_of, union_of, relationship (BFO:0000050 part_of, BFO:0000051 has_part, RO CURIEs in envo.obo), subset, disjoint_from, created_by/creation_date, is_obsolete/replaced_by/consider.

title: NCI Thesaurus (NCIt), flat file
publisher: National Cancer Institute, Enterprise Vocabulary Services (EVS)
perspective: NCI EVS (US federal government, NIH; cancer research and clinical vocabulary)
notes: Zip holds Thesaurus.txt, tab-delimited, no header row: code, concept IRI, parents (pipe-separated codes), synonyms (pipe-separated; first = preferred name), definition (one), display name, concept status, semantic type(s), concept in subset. Stated hierarchy only (no inferred relations); retired concepts carry a status. Identical versioned copy Thesaurus_26.08e.FLAT.zip; OWL editions also offered; current version via https://evs.nci.nih.gov/ftp1/thesaurus-latest (JSON). 'NCI Thesaurus' is a trademark. The OBO edition http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ncit.obo is 248,162,694 B and older (Last-Modified 2026-03-20). The EVS FTP page is now a JavaScript browser; the file URLs above are those named in the ReadMe.

title: NCBI Taxonomy database dump (taxdump)
publisher: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI), US National Library of Medicine
perspective: NCBI/NLM (US federal government; organisms with sequence data in the INSDC databases)
license: No restrictions: 'NCBI itself places no restrictions on the use or distribution of the data' (US government)
update: daily or more often (observed: rebuilt twice on 2026-09-25, last at 20:30 GMT)
notes: Size changes with every rebuild (79,614,555 B at 19:30 GMT, 79,615,599 B at 20:30 GMT on 2026-09-25): verify against the .md5 file fetched at the same time. Members: nodes.dmp, names.dmp, division.dmp, gencode.dmp, merged.dmp, delnodes.dmp, citations.dmp, images.dmp, readme.txt. Rows end with tab-pipe-newline and fields are separated by tab-pipe-tab, so it is not plain TSV. nodes: tax_id, parent tax_id, rank, embl code, division id, inherited flags, genetic code ids, GenBank hidden flag, hidden subtree flag, comments. names: tax_id, name_txt, unique name, name class (scientific name, synonym, common name, genbank common name, authority...). merged.dmp and delnodes.dmp keep id history for stable crosswalks. languages=2: scientific names plus (mostly English) common names. new_taxdump/new_taxdump.tar.gz (162,022,066 B) adds rankedlineage, fullnamelineage, taxidlineage, typematerial and more. The OBO derivative ncbitaxon (CC0) is on the OBO Foundry.

title: Catalogue of Life (COL) Base Release, ColDP
publisher: Catalogue of Life (COL), distributed via ChecklistBank
perspective: COL partnership (international network of taxonomic expert databases; COL Foundation, Amsterdam; GBIF-hosted infrastructure)
update: monthly releases, annual checklists since 2000; current Base Release 2026-09-11 (COL26.9)
notes: Open and unique but over the 500 MB bar (1.02 GB zipped; NameUsage.tsv alone 1.9 GB): 5,432,444 names, 2,269,433 species, 160 sources (ChecklistBank dataset 316321, DOI 10.48580/dgz5n, metadata.yaml license 'cc by'). Zip members: NameUsage.tsv (col:ID, col:parentID, col:basionymID, col:status, col:scientificName, col:authorship, col:rank, ..., col:extinct, plus denormalised kingdom..genus columns), VernacularName.tsv (col:taxonID, col:name, col:transliteration, col:language ISO 639-3, col:country...; 105 languages counted), Distribution.tsv, NameRelation.tsv, TypeMaterial.tsv, SpeciesEstimate.tsv, Reference.tsv, reference.json/.jsonl/.bib, metadata.yaml, source/<id>.yaml per source dataset. languages=106: 105 vernacular languages plus scientific names. Extended Release xr_latest_coldp.zip (1,255,670,027 B; 8.1M names) is now GBIF's default taxonomy; latest_txtree.zip (52,764,602 B) is an indented name tree without identifiers. www.catalogueoflife.org HTML pages answer 403 to non-browser user agents; the download host does not.

title: GBIF Backbone Taxonomy (legacy, frozen 2023-08-28)
perspective: GBIF (intergovernmental biodiversity data network, Copenhagen)
update: frozen: last build 2023-08-28; GBIF data blog (2026-06-23): 'will not be updated again', GBIF.org now defaults to COL XR
notes: Superseded: use the Catalogue of Life (Extended Release) for new work; keep only to resolve legacy GBIF taxonKeys, which GBIF still supports in its API. Darwin Core Archive with 13,320 members: Taxon.tsv (2.25 GB uncompressed), VernacularName.tsv (taxonID, vernacularName, language ISO 639-1, country, countryCode, sex, lifeStage, source; 155 languages counted), Distribution.tsv, Description.tsv, Multimedia.tsv, Reference.tsv, TypesAndSpecimen.tsv, eml.xml, dataset/<uuid>.xml per constituent. Built on COL July 2023. Also simple.txt.gz (488,591,022 B) in the same folder. languages=156: 155 vernacular languages plus scientific names.

title: ICD-11 for Mortality and Morbidity Statistics (MMS), simple tabulation 2026-01
perspective: WHO (UN specialized agency, Geneva; the international standard for health statistics reporting)
license: CC BY-ND 3.0 IGO under the WHO ICD-11 terms of use (crosswalks and translations need a separate WHO agreement)
notes: Licence blocks an open derived catalogue: no adaptations; incorporation in software is allowed only if WHO code, title and URI are kept; 'mapping or producing crosswalks between other classifications and terminologies and Classifications and producing translations are not covered' and need a separate written WHO agreement (terms 1.2.4) - which is exactly what acatalogue does. Zip: SimpleTabulation-ICD-11-MMS-en.txt (tab-delimited, 11.7 MB, header row: Foundation URI, Linearization URI, Code, BlockId, Title (prefixed by '- ' per depth, strip it), ClassKind chapter/block/category, DepthInKind, IsResidual, ChapterNo, BrowserLink (spreadsheet formula), isLeaf, Primary tabulation, Grouping1-5, CodingNote, Parent (foundation URI)), .xlsx copy, readme.txt. One zip per language: the browser lists ar cs de en es fr kk la pt ru sk sv tr uz zh and all 15 files answered 200. mapping.zip (6,809,366 B) holds ICD-10 to ICD-11 tables. The ICD API needs registration (client credentials).

title: SNOMED CT International Edition
perspective: SNOMED International (member-funded not-for-profit standards body, London; national release centres)
license: SNOMED CT Affiliate Licence (proprietary; no charge in member countries, charges may apply in non-member territories)
update: periodic International Edition releases via MLDS (cadence not checked)
verified: HEAD 200 2026-09-25 (MLDS portal page; files behind login)
notes: Restricted: use requires an Affiliate Licence registered with the member country's National Release Centre or with MLDS (Member Licensing and Distribution Service); non-member territories may pay fees set by World Bank income band. Content cannot be redistributed in an open catalogue. The URL is the MLDS portal (files behind login). Distributed as RF2: tab-delimited Snapshot/Full files (sct2_Concept, sct2_Description, sct2_Relationship, language and other refsets). languages=2: International Edition English plus SNOMED International's Spanish Edition; national extensions add others (not verified). The Global Patient Set (snomed.org/gps) is usable without a SNOMED licence but is CC BY-ND 4.0 behind a request form. Practical route: keep SNOMED ids that open ontologies already carry as xrefs (SCTID, SNOMEDCT_US_*).

title: UMLS Metathesaurus 2026AA (MRCONSO subset)
perspective: NLM (US federal government; integrates about 195 biomedical source vocabularies)
license: UMLS Metathesaurus License Agreement (free; per-source restriction levels 0-4 and 9)
notes: Needs a UTS account and licence acceptance: the download redirects to uts.nlm.nih.gov login (NLM documents API-key downloads). Restriction levels: 0 no extra restriction; 1 no translation or derivative works of that source; 2 also no operational data-creating use; 3 internal research use only, never in publicly accessible systems; 4 US-only use; 9 (19.56% of names; SNOMED CT). At most level-0 content could enter a public catalogue, source by source. Sizes per NLM page (no Content-Length before login): MRCONSO 492.0 MB zipped / 2.2 GB, Level 0 subset 1.9 GB, full subset 5.4 GB; MD5 values are printed on the page (MRCONSO 974beae09581ca990c764a511cce6563), no checksum file. MRCONSO.RRF is pipe-delimited: CUI|LAT|TS|LUI|STT|SUI|ISPREF|AUI|SAUI|SCUI|SDUI|SAB|TTY|CODE|STR|SRL|SUPPRESS|CVF|. 2026AA: 3,530,466 concepts, 18,064,970 names, 31 languages. MeSH (a level-0 UMLS source) is covered by the library-thesauri cluster.

title: QUDT units, quantity kinds, dimensions and constants (single-file collection 3.5.2)
perspective: QUDT.org (non-profit governed by a board from several organisations; engineering and data-exchange practice)
license: CC BY 4.0 (UCUM codes inside remain under the Regenstrief/UCUM licence)
notes: 'OWL schemas and vocabularies QUDT Collection - Version 3.5.2' (QUDT catalog). Per-graph Turtle: http://qudt.org/3.5.2/vocab/unit (4,094,284 B; 2,244 qudt:Unit) and http://qudt.org/3.5.2/vocab/quantitykind (1,859,462 B); unversioned http://qudt.org/vocab/unit always serves the latest. Not SKOS: units are qudt:Unit with rdfs:label in 24 languages (en de fr it es tr sl ro pl ms cs pt la ru el bg hu fa zh ar ja hi he nl), qudt:symbol, qudt:ucumCode, qudt:hasQuantityKind, qudt:conversionMultiplier(SN), qudt:hasDimensionVector, dcterms:description (LaTeX), crosswalks qudt:wikidataMatch, qudt:dbpediaMatch, qudt:iec61360Code, qudt:uneceCommonCode, qudt:omUnit, qudt:siExactMatch; deprecation via qudt:deprecated and dcterms:isReplacedBy. dcterms:rights states the UCUM notice (unitsofmeasure.org). Lean OBO alternative: UO, http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/uo.obo (124,858 B, CC BY 3.0).

title: Unified Astronomy Thesaurus (UAT) 6.0.0
perspective: AAS with IAU, IOP and AIP partners (learned societies and publishers; astronomy literature indexing)
update: versioned releases; 6.0.0 of 2025-12-16 (6.1.0 announced for spring 2026, not yet published)
notes: The repository listing (github.com/astrothesaurus/UAT) shows UAT.rdf, UAT.json, UAT.csv (337,607 B), UAT_list.json, UAT_simple.json; the v6.0.0 release has no data assets, so files come from the master branch - pin a commit for provenance. SKOS RDF/XML exported from PoolParty: statements about one concept are split over several rdf:Description blocks, so parse as RDF and merge by URI (http://astrothesaurus.org/uat/<n>). 2,312 concepts, 11 top concepts, polyhierarchy up to 11 levels, 696 related links (6.0.0 notes). Properties: skos:prefLabel/altLabel (@en, a few @en-GB), broader/narrower/related, skos:definition, scopeNote, example, changeNote, editorialNote, owl:deprecated. ShareAlike: tables derived from it must stay CC BY-SA.

title: NASA GCMD Science Keywords (KMS, SKOS) version 24.8
publisher: NASA Earth Science Data and Information System (ESDIS), Global Change Master Directory
perspective: NASA ESDIS (US federal space agency; Earth-observation data discovery)
license: CC0 1.0 (unless content is marked with a use restriction or licence)
notes: Redirects to cmr.earthdata.nasa.gov/kms; the KMS answers HEAD with 404 but GET with 200. Paginated: 3,780 concepts, page_size at most 2000, so fetch &page_num=1 and &page_num=2 (bytes = page 1). SKOS: skos:prefLabel (@en, upper case), broader/narrower, skos:definition for most concepts, gcmd:reference, changeNote history, dcterms:created/modified; concept ids are UUIDs relative to https://gcmd.earthdata.nasa.gov/kms/concept/. Single-file alternative ?format=csv (504,840 B; columns Category, Topic, Term, Variable_Level_1-3, Detailed_Variable, UUID; first line is version metadata; no definitions). Other schemes on the same API (platforms, instruments, locations, providers, projects, chronounits...) are listed at /kms/concept_schemes. Cite as 'GCMD Keywords, Version 24.8'.

title: SWEET - Semantic Web for Earth and Environmental Terminology 3.6.0
perspective: ESIP (US-based federation of Earth-science data organisations; originally NASA JPL)
notes: sweetAll is only a Turtle manifest (8,417 B measured; chunked, no Content-Length) whose owl:imports list 224 module ontologies (e.g. http://sweetontology.net/phenAtmo, realmHydro, matrElement), each served separately as Turtle (sources in src/*.ttl on GitHub): merge with ROBOT or fetch every import. About 6,000 OWL classes (README) with rdfs:label @en and rdfs:subClassOf hierarchy plus OWL restrictions. Open licence, but the modular OWL format is the obstacle and coverage overlaps ENVO and GCMD.

title: IPCC AR6 WGI reference regions v4 (GeoJSON)
publisher: IPCC Working Group I Atlas (with Santander Meteorology Group)
perspective: IPCC WGI (intergovernmental body under UNEP/WMO; climate assessment regions)
notes: 58 features (43 Land, 12 Ocean, 3 Land-Ocean; the README prose says 46 land and 14 ocean - trust the file) with properties Continent, Type, Name, Acronym and polygon geometry. Same regions as vertex CSV: IPCC-WGI-reference-regions-v4_coordinates.csv (6,429 B; Continent/Ocean, Surface, Reference region name, Acronym, Vertex1..n as lon|lat). The folder also holds WGII continental regions, monsoons, river basins, small islands and ocean biomes (GeoJSON plus shapefile zips). Licence from the Zenodo archive of the repository (record 5171760); the GitHub repo shows no LICENSE file. Iturbide et al. 2020, doi:10.5194/essd-12-2959-2020. Climate regions for the space facet.

title: OEIS sequence names (names.gz)
perspective: OEIS Foundation (US non-profit; volunteer-edited mathematical reference)
notes: Gzipped text: 4 comment lines starting with #, then one line per sequence 'A000001 Number of groups of order n.' (A-number, space, name). Companion stripped.gz (33,673,508 B, daily) holds the leading terms as ',0,1,1,1,2,...'; the full internal format is in github.com/oeis/oeisdata. EULA: credit 'The Online Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences' with a URL; non-share-alike use needs an arrangement with the OEIS Foundation. A-numbers are the de facto identifiers of integer sequences (Wikidata OEIS ID).

title: PubChem Periodic Table (element properties, CSV)
publisher: PubChem, National Center for Biotechnology Information (NLM/NIH)
perspective: NCBI/NLM (US federal government; compiled from IUPAC, NIST, IAEA and US DOE laboratory sources)
license: US government work (NLM): not subject to copyright in the US, acknowledge NLM; some underlying sources carry their own terms
notes: 15,017 B measured (chunked, no Content-Length). 118 rows; columns AtomicNumber, Symbol, Name, AtomicMass, CPKHexColor, ElectronConfiguration, Electronegativity, AtomicRadius, IonizationEnergy, ElectronAffinity, OxidationStates, StandardState, MeltingPoint, BoilingPoint, Density, GroupBlock, YearDiscovered; JSON at .../periodictable/JSON. Per-element provenance via PUG-View (/rest/pug_view/data/element/<n>/JSON) names IAEA AMDC, IUPAC CIAAW, Jefferson Lab, LANL, NIST PML, the IUPAC Periodic Table of the Elements and Isotopes (IUPAC contribution CC BY-NC-ND 4.0) and 'PubChem Elements' (NLM copyright page); check a value's source before republishing IUPAC-attributed data. PUG-View throttles (503 PUGVIEW.ServerBusy) - back off. IUPAC itself publishes no open bulk element table.

title: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology (Gold Book), all terms JSON
publisher: International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC)
perspective: IUPAC (international scientific union; normative chemical terminology)
license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (as stated in the Gold Book API metadata); whole-collection reuse by arrangement with IUPAC
update: not verified (site unreachable from this container)
notes: Blocked here: every goldbook.iupac.org URL answered 403 with a Cloudflare 'Just a moment' challenge (curl and WebFetch). IUPAC's own FAIR Chemistry Cookbook documents this endpoint (about 7,000 terms, about 804 kB) and quotes the API metadata: 'Licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NoDerivatives (CC BY-NC-ND) 4.0 International' and 'For parties interested in reusing the entire IUPAC Gold Book please contact IUPAC'. NonCommercial + NoDerivatives rule it out for an open catalogue. Per-term JSON at /terms/view/<code>/json (codes like C01093).

title: Our World in Data - CO2 and Greenhouse Gas Emissions dataset
publisher: Our World in Data (Global Change Data Lab)
perspective: OWID (Global Change Data Lab, UK non-profit; secondary compiler of Global Carbon Project, Jones et al., EIA and Energy Institute data)
license: CC BY 4.0 for data produced by OWID; third-party data keep their original licences
notes: One row per location and year: country, year, iso_code, population, gdp, cement_co2, co2, co2_per_capita, consumption_co2, cumulative_co2, coal/gas/oil/flaring/luc CO2, other greenhouse gases, energy per capita... Per-column description and source in owid-co2-codebook.csv (also a sheet in the XLSX) - use it to attribute each claim; XLSX and JSON variants are linked in the README. Locations mix countries with aggregates (World, continents, income groups): filter on iso_code. OWID's wider catalog is per-table Parquet/Feather at https://catalog.ourworldindata.org/<channel>/<dataset>/<version>/<dataset>/<table>.parquet (docs.owid.io Tables API; no single bulk file, bucket root 404) and per-chart CSV through the Chart API; most OWID indicators are third-party data under their own licences (OWID FAQ).

title: UN Global SDG Indicators Database, series-level archive (CSV)
perspective: UNSD (UN Secretariat, New York; official figures reported by countries and custodian agencies)
license: No open licence stated; the portal links the general UN website terms of use (personal, non-commercial use; no redistribution or derivative works)
update: archive snapshots several times a year; latest 2026-08-24
notes: Not a plain GET: POST multipart form field archiveId=<id> to this URL, as the portal's JavaScript does; list snapshots with POST .../ArchiveData/GetArchiveTable. Latest: archiveId 80 'Series Level' (2026-08-24, 84,485,510 B, text/csv) and 81 'Disaggregated Country Level' (131,928,891 B). The indicator framework is a lean GET: https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/UNSDGAPIV5/v1/sdg/Goal/List?includechildren=true (JSON: 17 goals, 169 targets, 251 indicator entries with code, title/description, tier). title: UN World Population Prospects 2024 - demographic indicators, medium variant (CSV)
perspective: UN DESA Population Division (UN Secretariat, New York; official UN population estimates and projections)
update: revision every 2-3 years (2019, 2022, 2024 current); interim Togo update 2026-01-22
notes: Gzipped UTF-8 CSV with BOM, 65 columns: SortOrder, LocID, Notes, ISO3_code, ISO2_code, SDMX_code, LocTypeID, LocTypeName, ParentID, Location, VarID, Variant, Time, TPopulation1Jan, TPopulation1July, ..., LEx, IMR, Q5, NetMigrations, CNMR; estimates 1950-2023 and medium projection 2024-2100 for countries and aggregates (LocTypeName tells them apart; for countries/areas LocID is the UN M49 numeric code - checked AFG 4, CHN 156, JPN 392, UZB 860 - matching space/m49-*, but ParentID points to WPP-specific region ids such as 906, and special aggregates such as ADB or AU regions come first with blank SortOrder). The .gz is multi-member (many concatenated gzip members): use a reader that continues past the first member. Location values containing commas are quoted. The site is a JavaScript app; file list and licence text come from /wpp/assets/downloads.json: TotalPopulationBySex.csv.gz (16,980,593 B), single-age and 5-year population, fertility, life tables, other variants; WPP2024_Locations_notes.csv (6,170 B); WPP2024_CSV_files_update.zip (943,827 B, 2026-01-22) corrects Togo only. A candidate replacement for the World Bank population baseline used by acat audit. Same URL as un-wpp2024-demographic-indicators in c-places-languages-time.tsv: keep one.

title: Eurostat database table of contents (bulk download inventory)
perspective: Eurostat (EU statistical office, Luxembourg; European Statistical System)
license: Re-use authorised with source acknowledgement (Commission Decision 2011/833/EU; editorial content CC BY 4.0); no commercial re-use of third-party or non-EU/EFTA/candidate-country data
notes: 1,972,798 B measured (chunked, no Content-Length). Quoted TSV: title (indented 4 spaces per level = the theme tree), code, type (1,924 folder / 8,875 dataset / 1,447 table), last update of data, last table structure change, data start, data end, values. lang=de and lang=fr return German and French titles (2,113,270 and 2,159,945 B); XML at .../toc/xml. Data are downloaded per dataset from the bulk download facility (gzip TSV, SDMX-CSV or SDMX 2.1) together with code lists and reference metadata; there is no single all-data file. Useful as a classification of official statistics (economy, population, environment, science and technology) to crosswalk with ACAT domains.

title: IANA Media Types registry
perspective: IANA (internet registry operator affiliated with ICANN; IETF standards process)
license: CC0 1.0 (IANA/IETF joint statement on the protocol registries, 2021)
notes: XML with 11 sub-registries (application, audio, example, font, haptics, image, message, model, multipart, text, video) and 2,361 <record>s: <name> (subtype), <file type='template'> (type/subtype), <xref> to RFCs or registrants, optional date attributes; a <people> section lists registrants. Per-type CSVs such as https://www.iana.org/assignments/media-types/application.csv (Name, Template, Reference). Small, stable identifiers for file-format concepts.

title: Unicode Character Database (UCD) 18.0.0
perspective: Unicode Consortium (US non-profit, industry-led; the universal character-encoding standard)
update: one major version a year; 18.0.0 files dated 2026-09-01
notes: 'latest' now points to 18.0.0; the pinned copy https://www.unicode.org/Public/18.0.0/ucd/UCD.zip is identical in size (5,657,953 B) - prefer it for provenance. 74 members, semicolon-delimited text: UnicodeData.txt (code point; name; general category; ...), NameAliases.txt, Blocks.txt, Scripts.txt, ScriptExtensions.txt, PropertyValueAliases.txt (script and category names), plus emoji/ and extracted/ folders. Character names are English by design; CJK readings and definitions are in Unihan.zip (8,340,649 B). Blocks + Scripts + PropertyValueAliases give a clean writing-system vocabulary for acat/language, keyed by ISO 15924 codes.

title: GitHub Linguist languages.yml (programming, markup, data and prose languages)
perspective: GitHub, Inc. (Microsoft-owned code-hosting company; languages as detected in code repositories)
notes: YAML mapping, one key per language: 836 (563 programming, 184 data, 71 markup, 18 prose) with type, language_id (stable integer), aliases, extensions, filenames, interpreters, group (parent language - the only hierarchy), color, tm_scope, ace_mode, codemirror_mode/codemirror_mime_type, wrap, fs_name.
